what: A .7 dark overlay covers the whole panel, and a flashlight circle follows the mouse position by .1 each frame (radius = Only a small area (short side × .3, blur × .375) is lit — hovering the evidence (spot) narrows the circle to 5/7 (.75s power3.out, release 1s power2.out), when turned on it flickers in like a bulb for .5s (rough 15 points), and every 10–20s it relights from .25 and blinks .35/.9s (rough 10 points). On touch devices it is fixed at the center.
ease: rough({ template: none.in, strength: 2, points: 10, taper: none, randomize: true, clamp: true })

options.shrink: Circle size multiplier when hovering evidence, default .714 (7 → 5)
options.intro: If off, bright right away with no turn-on
options.flicker: If off, it doesn’t blink on its own

note: Dark color is --kf-bg. The veil is made as a child and laid on top (z 2), the marker for receiving interaction is data-fx-part="spot" — normally under the veil (z 1), and on hover or focus it floats above the veil (z 3) so it is also visible outside the circle — the original is WebGL post-processing (masking panel · glow panel), so letting the evidence show through above the veil is replaced with z. Without EasePack, GSAP cannot read the curve name instead of rough and warns, so load it together

from.where: index.js flashlight circle (flashMesh · post uFocusFactor) — original FakeFlashlight radius .2 · softness .25 · size 7→5 · mouse easing .1, animateFlashlightOn · Flicker
